texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 19.11.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 19.11.2023 at about 7.40 p.m., petitioner was riding a Motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 05-H-7550 from Vignan Nagar towards Annsandra Palya by wearing headguard slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing on moving vehicles, when he reached near Shall Petrol Bunk, at that time the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-01- NA-2834 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came at high speed from Jain Heights Apartments and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle. Due to forced impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, wherein he was treated as in-patient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 65 years, the petitioner was doing real estate business and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to do job and hence lost his earnings. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. 3. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court, hence placed exparte. Ravi Kumar vs Sharana Prasad Melkundi on 26 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128699695/ 2 The respondent No.2 filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. This respondent admits the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and liabilities if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 134(c), 158(6) and 170 of M. V. Act. This respondent specifically submits that car bearing reg. No. KA-01-NA-2834 was not involved in the accident and jurisdictional police have filed the false charge sheet against the insured vehicle by colluding with the petitioner without conducting the proper investigation. Further, this respondent submits that, at the time of alleged accident the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding Driving License to drive the vehicle, thereby the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14, examined one Vedavathi. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.15 and 16, examined Dr. S. Ramachandra as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.17 and 18 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of respondents.
texts.arguments: Hence, as per the decision reported in (1999) 3 SCC 573 between Vidhyadhar vs Manikrao & Anr. 16. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. It is further contended that, the injured petitioner was doing Real Estate Business and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month. But respondent No.2 disputed the income of petitioner, but no reliable evidence is produced by the petitioner to show how much income he was getting from his work. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
